In December 1952, two young Americans were reported lost on a flight from Korea to Japan.
John Downey and Richard Fecteau were CIA officers, shot down inside China.
Their job that night: pick up an agent from the snow, without landing.
Two poles held a line. The plane trails a hook, catches the line, and winches the man aboard.
But the agent team had been caught. The radio call was a trap.
Under a nearly full moon, the plane came in low and slow. White sheets flew off two hidden guns.
The plane crashed in the trees. Both pilots died. Downey and Fecteau lived.
A Chinese officer looked at Downey and said: You are Jack.
For twenty years, Washington stuck to its story.
Then President Nixon said it out loud: Downey involves a CIA agent.
Six weeks later, Downey walked across a bridge into Hong Kong, after seven thousand, four hundred and eight days.
